_comment: Rendering style config, shared between mapbuilder's webapp preview and (eventually) the xteink firmware renderer. Kept as flat tag->rule matching so a future C++ loader stays simple. Not the final on-device binary tile format (see roadmap item 13) -- this is the authoring/spec format. The device is strictly 1-bit e-ink (no anti-aliasing, no grayscale) -- every 'color' field is #000000; differentiate features by width/pattern/hatch only, never color. This file is the one and only style file -- there is no separate mapbuilder/style.json. It lives here, not in mapbuilder, because this repo builds from it and is the one that gets pushed (see xteink CLAUDE.md, 'This repo is never pushed anywhere').
_comment_when: PER MODE AND PER RUNG. Any object in this file may carry a `when` list: [{"modes": [...], "steps": [...], <fields to override>}]. `modes` omitted means every travel mode, `steps` omitted means every zoom rung (0-6, the ladder in docs/map-data-spec.md). Entries apply in order and the LAST matching one wins -- that is the whole precedence rule. scripts/mapstyle_variants.py evaluates them at firmware BUILD time and scripts/gen_mapstyle.py emits one finished MapStyle per distinct (mode, rung), plus an index; the device does one array lookup and never sees a rule (src/activities/map/MapStyleTable.h). `when` is banned under `device`: the marker anchor becomes a constexpr the viewport arithmetic is built on, so it cannot vary. Identical variants are deduplicated, so a style with no `when` at all costs one struct.

device._comment: 480x800 = PORTRAIT logical coords (CrossPointSettings.h ORIENTATION::PORTRAIT, the firmware default) -- NOT the raw 800x480 SSD1677 panel silicon, which is landscape-native but rotated by the renderer. marker_x_px/marker_y_px are the position puck's place on screen, in device pixels from the top-left; the viewport is whatever falls around it, asymmetric in both axes. This replaces marker_y_from_bottom_frac, which could only express a vertical offset -- on the device the marker slides across a stationary map to avoid a full e-ink refresh per GPS update, so it is free in both axes. See docs/map-render-spec.md.

buildings._comment: Building rings, rung 0 only. At 1 m/px a building is 21 px and is what the rider is looking at; at 3 m/px it is 7 px and measured 4,122 ms of that rung's 7,463 on hardware, which is 55% of the slowest rung for texture. Rungs 2-6 read tiles that carry no buildings at all (tilegen build_config.json), so false there only skips an empty pass. `enabled: false` means the layer is never opened, so a hidden rung costs no card read either. Moved here from MapViewport::ZoomStep::buildings 2026-08-25.

contours._comment: Elevation contours, tile layer_id 7, two classes. A contour is a line of equal height; an index contour is every Nth one, drawn heavier so the eye can count. The tiles carry 20 m lines at the detail LOD with every 5th (100 m) as index, and 100 m lines from regional out with every 5th (500 m) as index (mapbuilder/tilegen/build_config.json). Solid strokes only: a dithered 1 px line reads as dashed and a dashed contour reads as a footpath, so weight is the only separator there is. Drawn over the landuse wash and under buildings, water and roads -- a contour crossing a road must not break it. `enabled: false` for ride and cycle means the layer is never opened, so those modes pay no card read at all. Rung 1 draws only the index lines and rungs 5-6 only the 500 m ones: 20 m at 3 m/px and 100 m at 32-45 m/px are wall to wall on a mountain flank, measured on 480x800 1:1 renders 2026-08-26 (docs/contours-plan.md).

junctions._comment: Junction dots, drawn ONLY along the route. Three filters: within max_dist_px of the route; significant, i.e. require_major means at least one road there is flagged major in the roads layer and not hidden (otherwise every side street and footpath in a village beads the whole route); and no two closer than min_spacing_px along the route. Keyed on the roads layer's `major` flag, NOT on rule width -- width is cosmetic, so thinning the major roads must not silently delete the dots. halo_px is a white ring around each dot, without which they are invisible where they sit on the black route. Sizes in device pixels.

landuse._comment: Forest and built-up areas, one tile layer (layer_id 6), two classes. Drawn under everything else: built-up first, then forest, then water, buildings and roads on top. Each class gets its own fill because they are background tones and two adjacent tones that match make their boundary vanish.

offscreen_places._comment: Edge indicators for villages OUTSIDE the viewport. A clipped-away village tells you nothing, but 'which way is the next village' is exactly what a glance needs -- so each gets a chevron on the screen edge where the ray from the position marker exits, pointing outward, with the name pulled back inside so it cannot be clipped too. Nearest first: if two want the same piece of edge (closer than min_gap_px) the further one is dropped rather than overlapped, and at most max_count are shown. Sizes in device pixels.

places._comment: Village/town dot + label, all sizes in DEVICE PIXELS. Two tiers: label_px/label_bold draw city and town (place rank <= 1), label_minor_px/label_minor_bold everything smaller (village/suburb/hamlet/farm) -- size and weight carry the hierarchy. label_px and label_minor_px are LINE HEIGHTS in device pixels, not point sizes: the renderer picks the largest built-in face that fits (29 px gets the Ubuntu UI bold, 24 px its regular -- the smallest built-in Noto Sans is a 34 px line), since 1-bit e-ink has no colour and all-caps reads worse at a glance. Names stay in their own Title Case. Legibility over a road network comes from label_halo_px, a white outline around the glyphs; label_bg true replaces it with the older opaque white box (label_bg_pad_px, label_bg_border_px), which is stronger but eats a rectangle of map. Declutter: labels are placed rank-first and each is dropped if its measured box collides with a label already placed (inflated by min_label_gap_px) or covers more than max_route_overlap_pct of itself with the route -- the route is the one thing a label must not hide. max_labels is a render-cost cap, not the declutter mechanism. label_max_width_px truncates a long name with an ellipsis; the dot is always drawn even when the label is not. See firmware docs/place-labels.md and docs/map-render-spec.md item 5. label_char_width_frac is the laptop sketch's character-count width estimate only -- the device and the firmware preview both measure the real font. max_labels is per rung since 2026-08-25 (see _comment_when): 3 names at rung 0, which shows 480 x 800 m and one settlement, up to 14 at rung 6, which shows 24 x 40 km. Those numbers came from MapViewport::ZoomStep::maxLabels, where they were a second table beside this file.

points._comment: POI marks from the .tip point layer (safety points now, landmarks later). square/glyph/flag/cluster_* are DEVICE PIXELS: a mark is a screen decoration and must stay legible at every zoom rung, so it does not scale with mpp. square_px 0 hides the layer and the shards are then never opened. Sized 15/1/9/4 from a real-size render (MapPointMarks.h); grown 20 percent to 18/2/11/5 on the maintainer's call after seeing it on the panel 2026-08-22 -- the glyph shapes were judged at 9 px, so 11 px is a scale nobody has judged yet. cluster_radius_px/cluster_cell_px added 2026-08-25 for the 24px icon set's own clustering (docs/map-render-spec.md, "POI clustering") -- points within cluster_radius_px of each other on screen merge into one cluster_cell_px-celled tile.

position._comment: The 'you are here' puck at the viewport origin: white disc, black ring, black heading arrow. Sizes in device pixels.

roads._comment: Widths in DEVICE PIXELS (as is every length in this file). Rules match on `class`, the tile format's own class enum (mapbuilder/tilegen/class_spec.py) -- the same vocabulary `modes` uses -- not raw OSM `highway` tags; the tag-to-class mapping lives in mapbuilder/tilegen/tag_to_class.py. casing_px > 0 draws the road as two parallel black edges of that thickness with the road left white between them -- how a wide main road is distinguished from a thin one on 1-bit e-ink. `major` marks roads you would turn onto (the junctions layer keys off it, NOT off width, which is cosmetic). `hidden` means matched-but-not-drawn, and a class hidden at a rung is not even read off the card there -- gen_mode_masks.py intersects it out of that rung's class mask. Every class in the enum except `unknown` has a rule here; `unknown` is deliberately unstyled and falls to `default` below. The main classes carry a `when` list of per-rung widths (see _comment_when): a device pixel is 1 m of ground at rung 0 and 45 m at rung 6, so a fixed 11 px motorway is a 495 m band at the coarse end. The shape at the two widest rungs, measured on the Prague and Pezinok ladder references 2026-08-25: three cased weights for the roads you steer by (motorway, trunk, primary), a thin solid for the connecting network (secondary, 2 px), and a 1 px hairline for the mesh (tertiary; unclassified already was one). NEVER trade a casing for a thinner solid -- a casing inks two edges and leaves the middle white, so 4 px cased costs 2 px of black and 3 px solid costs 3, and doing it made rung 4 darker. motorway and trunk are drawn the way a paper map draws them since 2026-08-25: a 1 px outline with a SHADED middle, `fill: tone` plus `tone: light`, rather than two thick black edges around white. `light` is the period-2 dither (pixel, gap, pixel) -- the direct sibling of the `stipple` the built-up areas use, which is period 3. The weight comes from the fill now, so the casing drops from 2 px to 1 px. It costs LESS ink than the white version it replaced and reads as a ribbon instead of a band. `fill: tone` needs a casing and an interior of at least 2 px; gen_mapstyle.py refuses it otherwise rather than silently drawing nothing. UNVERIFIED on a panel: measured on the host renderer only.

route._comment: distinguished from roads by width alone -- there is no color on 1-bit e-ink. width/arrow_* are DEVICE PIXELS: screen decorations must stay legible at any map zoom, so they do not scale with mpp.

water._comment: Water lines and lake areas. Rules key on `class`, the water layer's own class byte (unknown/river/stream/lake, mapbuilder/water_class.py) -- NOT on OSM tags. The tile carries the class; matching tags here would be a second vocabulary nothing can check (docs/map-data-spec.md, 'One vocabulary, not two'). stream covers canal and drain. Only lake arrives as a ring, so only its rule needs a fill.

modes._comment: Render-time class filter, one entry per travel mode. This is the mode's VOCABULARY: which classes it cares about at all. What the tile reader actually filters with is this intersected with the classes that zoom rung's style draws, compiled by scripts/gen_mode_masks.py into a 32-bit mask per (mode, rung) at firmware build time; the device tests mask & (1 << class_id) -- there is no style file on the device and no load-time parsing. A way outside the mask is not read past its header. One tile set serves all three modes -- never filter by mode at build time (docs/map-data-spec.md, 'Mode is a render-time filter'). A `when` list works here too, for a mode whose vocabulary should narrow at the coarse rungs. Names are the tile format's own class enum (mapbuilder/tilegen/class_spec.py), not style rule names, so editing the style never forces a tile rebuild. An unknown name, or a mask that resolves to empty at any rung, fails the build.
